name: MARIAGENSPIEL (MARIAGE)
description: Mariagenspiel is the historical ancestor of the vast 'Marriage' family of card games, which includes global hits like Sixty-Six, Schnapsen, Pinochle, and Belote. Its name literally means 'Marriage Game', referring to the core mechanic: earning bonus points by holding and declaring a King and Queen of the same suit. It is a trick-taking game where players must balance the pursuit of card points with the opportunistic timing of their marriages.

content.text: Mariagenspiel is the historical ancestor of the vast 'Marriage' family of card games, which includes global hits like Sixty-Six, Schnapsen, Pinochle, and Belote. Its name literally means 'Marriage Game', referring to the core mechanic: earning bonus points by holding and declaring a King and Queen of the same suit. It is a trick-taking game where players must balance the pursuit of card points with the opportunistic timing of their marriages.
First appearing in French and German gaming books in the early 18th century (c. 1715). It set the standard for bonus-point declarations.

Two players. The game is played by two people; each receives six cards at the start. One card is turned face-up for trump (the seven of trumps may be exchanged for it). While the stock lasts, after each trick both players draw to refill to six cards.
Each player receives 6 cards. One card is flipped to determine the Trump suit.

items.text: Three-hand Mariage: Three players; 36 cards; 5 cards each; replenish after each trick. Marriage bonuses paid by each opponent. First to reach target wins.
Kreuzmariage (Cross Mariage): Four players, 8 cards each; last card to dealer sets trump. Melds declared at start in turn; winner has most card points; no matsch; slam earns 8 chips from each.
Closing the stock: A player may close the stock (turn-up crosswise on stock) to try to win from hand; phase 2 rules apply immediately. If closer fails, opponent wins the deal.
